summary: The first mismatch is attributed to teleport.c:collect_coords, but C reaches that RNG only after the coaligned altar prayer invokes pray_revive() and restores the tame pet from its corpse. JS prayer_done still skips this source branch with note_unported, so later prayer RNG is consumed where C revives the dog. The actionable owner is the whole pray.c:pray_revive helper and its prayer_done caller wiring.

source.branch: In prayer_done() p_type == 3 on a coaligned altar, the floor pile at the hero coordinates contains a corpse or statue with saved monster traits marked tame and not a minion.
callers: pray.c:prayer_done() p_type-3 altar arm calls (void) pray_revive() before (void) water_prayer(TRUE) at 2336-2338.
pray.c:dopray() installs prayer_done as the delayed prayer callback; the #pray command reaches it through the negative-multi countdown and hack.c:unmul().
dependencies: zap.c:revive() returns a monster pointer consumed by pray_revive() to produce its boolean result; the existing JS owner is zap.js:revive().
zap.c:montraits() restores saved corpse traits and returns the revived monster; JS zap.js:montraits() delegates creation through makemon_create.js:makemon_revival().
trap.c:animate_statue() is the other consumed-return callee for the statue arm; the existing JS owner is trap.js:animate_statue().

makemon.c:makemon() is reached beneath saved-trait restoration and its result is consumed by montraits(); worker B currently owns that whole-function reservation, so C scope remains pray.c:pray_revive unless source verification demonstrates that dependency needs expansion.

evidence: Queue provenance was refreshed after accepted B223 at game commit 07a45f0d02529c0ca8796e4a38578d49c418d1c3: v40/v40-coaligned-prayer-revives-tame-pet-corpse remains in .cache/latest-saved-combined-queue.json at SHA-256 d73bb8439f9c009e8a418bd7b866c843af46c9687faf20a01c71599e3362ba03 with 2 remaining screens and earliest mismatch step 41. The accepted evaluation records 41/43 screens, 2605/2655 RNG calls, and 42/43 cursors; it still reports C rn2(8)=3 from collect_coords(teleport.c:700), JS rn2(3)=0, and a C dog glyph where JS shows the floor.

C pray.c:pray_revive() (2177-2196) scans svl.level.objects[u.ux][u.uy] in linked-list order and accepts only CORPSE or STATUE objects with saved OMONST traits whose monster is tame and not a minion. The corpse arm returns revive(otmp, TRUE) != NULL; the statue arm returns animate_statue(otmp, u.ux, u.uy, ANIMATE_SPELL, NULL) != NULL.

C pray.c:prayer_done() (2336-2338) reaches pray_revive only in the p_type-3 coaligned arm when on_altar() is true, discards its boolean result, then calls water_prayer(TRUE). JS pray.js:prayer_done() currently records note_unported('pray.c pray_revive') at the same position before water_prayer(true), identifying the missing behavior and safe caller replacement.

The C step-41 random log continues after collect_coords with next_ident(mkobj.c:521), newmonhp(makemon.c:1042), makemon(makemon.c:1279), montraits(zap.c:750), and wary_dog(dog.c:1313). This is the source path for restoring the saved pet; collect_coords is reached inside revival placement rather than being the defective selection algorithm. The JS branch skips revival, then consumes rn2(3) in later prayer handling.

The independent JS implementations already present for the selected helper callees are zap.js:revive(), zap.js:montraits(), makemon_create.js:makemon_revival(), and trap.js:animate_statue(). B currently reserves source:makemon.c:makemon; the C task can remain bounded to pray.c:pray_revive and js/pray.js while declaring that existing caller dependency, unless focused source/runtime validation proves the makemon owner must change.
